history.summary: NOTE: CSV town 'Puri' is approximate - the temple is at Chaurasi village, Puri district, on the right bank of the Prachi river (~27-30 km from Konark, ~14 km from Kakatpur). East-facing sandstone shrine (approx 15.84 m x 8.23 m x 8.40 m) built in the rare Khakhara (Kharkhara) style used for goddess temples, maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India. The presiding deity is Matsya Varahi - pot-bellied, boar-faced, holding a fish in her right hand and a kapala in her left, with a third eye. She is worshipped with tantric rites and offered fish daily; erotic sculptures and Tantric/Vaishnav fusion imagery make it a key Kaula/Vamacara site. Chaurasi also has the Amareswar and Laxminarayan temples. Coordinates (20.0586, 86.1186) are from shreekhetra.com (20 deg 03'31"N 86 deg 07'07"E) - approximate, geocoder could not resolve Chaurasi precisely.

name: Varahi Temple
town_description: Chaurasi is a small village in Puri district on the right bank of the Prachi river, between Nimapada and Kakatpur. It is famous for the 10th-century Varahi (Barahi) Deula, a Tantric goddess shrine, and also hosts the Amareswar and Laxminarayan temples. Chaurasi sits within the Prachi Valley temple circuit, roughly 27-30 km from Konark.
